title: Pack the last two eggs small end down
instruction: Put the two loose eggs into the empty carton cups, small end down.
context: Egg graders and packers set eggs in cartons small end down so that the air cell at the blunt end stays up and the yolk stays centred, turning eggs that arrive lying on their side on end as they are set in a cup.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m; x forward from the arm bases, y to the left; arm bases at x 0, y +-0.305 m). Two loose large hen's eggs (egg_l at x = 0.22 m, y = +0.20 m and egg_r at x = 0.22 m, y = -0.20 m), each a 57 mm long by 44 mm equatorial diameter Hügelschäffer ovoid convex hull (egg.obj, w = 3 mm, small end at local +z, 58 g, cream shell colour 0.93, 0.87, 0.76), spawned lying horizontally along x with the small end pointing toward +x on a pair of fixed blue rubber cradle rails (two 40 x 6 x 8 mm rails per egg, inner faces 18 mm apart at y_egg +- 9 mm, colour 0.25, 0.45, 0.80). Forward at x = 0.34 m sits a fixed six-cup moulded-pulp carton row (colour 0.72, 0.68, 0.60): two empty end cups at (0.34, +0.20) m (cup_l) and (0.34, -0.20) m (cup_r), each a 60 x 60 x 35 mm pulp block with a 25 mm deep conical cup tapering from 46 mm diameter at the rim (z = 0.7825 m) to a 24 mm flat seat floor 10 mm above the table (z = 0.7575 m, exact triangle mesh carton.obj, approximation = 'none'); a 3 mm thick pulp bridging plate across the top from y = -0.17 m to +0.17 m, x = 0.31 to 0.37 m (z = 0.7795 to 0.7825 m, compound segments bridging the gaps between the six cup blocks); and four fixed inner cups at y = -0.105, -0.035, +0.035, and +0.105 m (x = 0.34 m) holding four fixed eggs (fixed_egg_1 to fixed_egg_4) already standing small end down; the inner cups are the same 60 x 60 x 35 mm moulded-pulp cups and the fixed eggs the same 57 x 44 mm hen's eggs as above. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The tilt of an egg is the angle between its small-end axis (local +z) and downward world -z (0 deg means small end straight down). A carton cup holds an egg leaning against its conical wall rather than upright (a correctly packed egg rests at ~13.3 deg), whereas an egg set blunt end down rests at 126-141 deg and an egg left on its cradle sits at ~71 deg. A loose egg (egg_l or egg_r) is packed in an empty cup (cup_l at (0.34, +0.20) m or cup_r at (0.34, -0.20) m) when all five conditions hold: (1) its centre xy is within 4.0 mm of that empty cup's axis; (2) its lowest point (world bounding-box low z) is below that cup's rim (0.7825 m, TOP + 0.035 m) and on the table; (3) its small-end axis (local +z) is within 20.0 deg of world -z; (4) it is at rest (resting(): linear speed under 1 cm/s and angular speed under 0.5 rad/s); and (5) it is released (both grippers' tool centre points at least 3.0 cm from every point of the egg's 44 x 44 x 57 mm bounding box). Each empty cup counts at most once. Score (SCORE_OVER = 'end'): 0.5 times the number of packed eggs (0.0, 0.5, or 1.0). Success is when both loose eggs are packed and holds for 1.0 s. Distance is the sum over the two loose eggs of the horizontal xy distance (m) to the nearer empty cup axis plus 0.001 m per degree of tilt above 20.0 deg.
fidelity: Each egg is one rigid convex hull (no shell compliance or cracking); the carton is two moulded cups with a bridging top plate and four fixed inner cups holding four fixed eggs, rather than a full 12-cup hinged carton; 'small end down' is defined as the long axis within 20 deg of vertical because conical carton cups hold eggs leaning (~13.3 deg at rest).
